clinical_note.name: Plan
items:
Work-related stress and anxiety:
- Continue to practice taking scheduled breaks during the workday
- Continue to practice leaving work on time, starting with Tuesday at 6 PM
- Practice distinguishing between being available and being helpful
- Develop a standardized response for after-hours client communication: "I received your message. I know this is stressful. I will review the details and call you tomorrow."
- Acknowledge that caring about work does not require treating every unanswered message as a test of character
- Remind self that leaving work on time does not mean stopped caring
- Discussed the distinction between being available (responding immediately) and being helpful (doing the next appropriate thing)
- Explored the connection between current work patterns and childhood experiences with father's illness
- Discussed that caring deeply does not require becoming the whole system
- Explored the concept of making room for both truths: having been strained and less available, while taking steps to reconnect
- Discussed that letting grief exist does not make one incapable of continuing work
- Continue to monitor for suicidal ideation and self-harm risk
- Review progress with boundary-setting and work-life balance at next session
Grief:
- Continue to allow grief to arise naturally without treating it as a problem to solve
- Discussed that letting the feeling exist did not make the patient incapable of continuing work
- Explored the connection between father's organization and patient's current work patterns
- Discussed that staying vigilant is not the only way to show care
